title: The Unlikely Villain of the Midterms

source.title: Voters rebuff data centers in every ballot measure except one during the 2026 midterms

background_ko: 데이터센터는 AI를 돌리는 거대한 서버 건물입니다. 전기와 냉각용 물을 엄청나게 씁니다. 미국에서는 AI 붐으로 데이터센터가 빠르게 늘었고, 2026년 11월 중간선거 때 여러 지역이 데이터센터 건설을 막거나 제한할지 주민투표에 부쳤습니다.
warmup_q: 우리 동네에 대형 데이터센터가 들어온다면 찬성할까요, 반대할까요? 이유는?

lines.en: For years, / data centers were the **quiet** engines / of the digital economy.
lines.ko: 수년간 데이터센터는 디지털 경제의 조용한 엔진이었다.

lines.en: Few people noticed them, / and even fewer **objected to** them.
lines.ko: 그것을 알아차리는 사람은 거의 없었고, 반대하는 사람은 더더욱 적었다.

lines.en: That changed dramatically / in this month's U.S. midterm elections.
lines.ko: 이번 달 미국 중간선거에서 그것이 극적으로 바뀌었다.

lines.en: Voters in ten states / weighed in on 41 local measures / involving data centers.
lines.ko: 10개 주의 유권자들이 데이터센터와 관련된 41건의 지역 안건에 의견을 표했다.

lines.en: In 40 of them, / the result went **against** the facilities.
Some measures **banned** new construction outright, / while others **put** projects **on hold**.
lines.ko: 어떤 안건은 신규 건설을 전면 금지했고, 다른 안건은 사업을 보류시켰다.

lines.en: The **backlash** was driven / largely by rising electricity bills.
lines.ko: 이 반발은 주로 오르는 전기 요금 때문에 일어났다.

lines.en: A single large data center / can **consume** as much power as a small city.
lines.ko: 대형 데이터센터 하나는 작은 도시만큼의 전력을 소비할 수 있다.

lines.en: Residents also worried about water use, / noise, / and the **impact** on local land.
lines.ko: 주민들은 물 사용, 소음, 지역 토지에 미치는 영향도 우려했다.

lines.en: Polls showed / that people opposed new data centers in their communities / by roughly three to one.
lines.ko: 여론조사에 따르면 사람들은 자기 지역의 신규 데이터센터에 약 3대 1로 반대했다.

lines.en: Many of the votes were **non-binding**, / so they cannot stop projects **on their own**.
lines.ko: 상당수 투표는 구속력이 없어서, 그 자체만으로는 사업을 막을 수 없다.

lines.en: Still, / the message to the tech industry / was **hard to ignore**.
lines.ko: 그래도 기술 업계에 전달된 메시지는 무시하기 어려웠다.

lines.en: Within days, / some AI companies promised / to **pay for** their own power / and to be more open with neighbors.
lines.ko: 며칠 만에 일부 AI 기업들은 자체 전력 비용을 부담하고 이웃 주민들에게 더 투명하게 하겠다고 약속했다.

lines.en: Others insisted / they would **keep investing**, / arguing that AI needs this infrastructure to grow.
lines.ko: 다른 기업들은 AI가 성장하려면 이 인프라가 필요하다며 투자를 계속하겠다고 고집했다.

lines.en: Either way, / the era of building data centers / **without asking permission** / may be over.
lines.ko: 어느 쪽이든, 허락을 구하지 않고 데이터센터를 짓던 시대는 끝났을지도 모른다.

words.example: Local residents **objected to** the new highway.
The city passed a **measure** to limit noise at night.
Several countries have **banned** single-use plastic bags.
The price hike caused a strong **backlash** from customers.
Older refrigerators **consume** a lot of electricity.
Social media has a huge **impact** on teenagers.
The survey results are **non-binding**, but managers will consider them.
The government plans to invest in **infrastructure** like roads and bridges.
We are living in the **era** of artificial intelligence.

idioms.example: Experts were invited to **weigh in on** the new policy.
We had to **put** our travel plans **on hold**.
The final decision **went against** the company.
A good idea alone can't succeed **on its own**.
Take the bus or the subway. **Either way**, you'll be late.

key_sentences.en: Few people noticed them, and **even fewer** objected to them.
key_sentences.note: few(거의 없는) → even fewer(훨씬 더 적은). 비교급 강조에는 even, much, far, still을 씁니다.

key_sentences.en: A single large data center can consume **as much power as** a small city.
key_sentences.note: as much + 명사 + as A: A만큼 많은 ~. 셀 수 있는 명사라면 as many ~ as를 씁니다.

key_sentences.en: The backlash **was driven** largely **by** rising electricity bills.
key_sentences.note: 수동태 be driven by: ~에 의해 촉발되다. 원인을 말할 때 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 표현입니다.

key_sentences.en: Others insisted they would keep investing, **arguing that** AI needs this infrastructure.
key_sentences.note: 분사구문 ~ing: 동시에 일어나는 동작이나 이유를 덧붙입니다(= and they argued that ...).

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: AI companies stopped building data centers.
Voters strongly pushed back against data centers in the midterms.
Data centers use less power than people think.
All data center votes are legally binding.

questions.q: What was the main reason for the backlash?
Why can't many of the votes stop projects on their own?
T / F : Every tech company promised to stop investing in data centers.
questions.answer: F — 일부는 투자를 계속하겠다고 했다. (14번 문장)

blanks.sentence: The new law will ________ smoking in all public parks.
The company faced a huge ________ after raising its prices.
Due to the storm, the concert was put on ________.
Many people were asked to weigh ________ on the decision.
Electric cars ________ less energy than gasoline cars.

output_task:
🗣 Speak: 1~4번 문장을 3번씩 소리 내어 읽고, / 표시에서 짧게 끊어 쉐도잉하세요.
✍️ Write (2~3문장): Would you support a data center in your town? Why or why not? → 오늘 배운 object to, impact, either way 중 2개 이상 사용하기.
